kept.claim: When recovery codes are written to user storage, any existing Keycloak-stored recovery-authn-codes credential is left in place, and UserCredentialManager.isValid falls back to the local validator, so the old codes still work after regeneration.
kept.evidence: CredentialHelper.java:126-131 only logs on the user-storage path. Old-credential deletion exists only in RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential (lines 39-40). UserCredentialManager.isValid:59-80 leaves a code the federated validator rejected in toValidate, then runs local validators; RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid:99-118 accepts the stale local credential's next code. Before this PR all users' recovery codes went through createCredential, so upgraded users have stale local credentials. Limit: only the next unused old code in order is accepted, not any old code.

kept.claim: For a user-storage credential, the exhausted-codes cleanup at line 86 still calls removeStoredCredentialById, which only touches Keycloak's JPA store; with a provider-returned credential that has no id, that passes null to em.find and can throw during login.
kept.evidence: RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:80 prefers the federated credential, but :86 calls removeStoredCredentialById, which only reaches the JPA store (UserCredentialManager.java:114-117). The createFromValues model has a null id. Overstated: unreachable with the PR's reference provider, and :90-92 still adds CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES, which replaces the credential through user storage.
kept.corrected_claim: For a user-storage credential, the exhausted-codes cleanup at line 86 still calls removeStoredCredentialById, which only touches Keycloak's JPA store; with a provider-returned credential that has no id, that passes null to em.find and can throw during login.

dropped.claim: Core code now parses a user-storage credential with createFromCredentialModel, which needs Keycloak-format secretData/credentialData JSON; a provider returning a plain recovery-authn-codes CredentialModel gets an unchecked exception (HTTP 500) on the login page.
dropped.evidence: Not a regression. Before this PR, RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean used getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...).findFirst().get(), so user-storage recovery codes already failed with a 500. It needs a hypothetical provider that returns a recovery-authn-codes credential in a non-Keycloak format; the only reference provider uses createFromValues.

dropped.claim: The reference user storage accepts any of the 12 codes and never uses one up, so codes can be replayed without limit and the prompted code number (always #1) does not match what is validated; the new test logs in only once, so it cannot catch this.
dropped.evidence: The mechanics are accurate (anyMatch with no consumption, prompt always shows #1), but the code is a testsuite fixture and not shipped. Production paths are unaffected, and consuming codes is the provider's responsibility.

dropped.claim: The provider now stores recovery codes but disableCredentialType and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream handle only OTP, so user-storage recovery codes cannot be removed from the account console or admin API, and the returned credential has no id, so CredentialDeleteHelper cannot match it.
dropped.evidence: The facts hold (disableCredentialType and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream are OTP-only, null id), but they are limited to the test fixture, and the PR does not claim to support removing user-storage recovery codes.
